revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Real Estate
revealWordProblem.text: Terrance is helping his grandmother sell her house. He uses a real estate website to look at the recent sale prices of similarly‑sized houses in their area and collects the prices in the table shown. What would be a fair, but competitive, selling price for Terrance’s grandmother’s house? Use the median to justify your answer.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A real-estate sign reading Sold, showing a table of sixteen recent house sale prices.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort the 16 sale prices from least to greatest: $160,000, $199,900, $239,900, $269,900, $307,000, $382,900, $385,400, $401,785, $402,400, $405,400, $423,400, $426,400, $454,400, $457,400, $460,400, $485,250. With 16 values (an even number), the median is the average of the 8th and 9th values: ($401,785 + $402,400) ÷ 2 = $804,185 ÷ 2 = $402,092.50. A fair, competitive selling price would be around $402,000, since that's the middle of the market and isn't pulled up or down by the lowest sale ($160,000) or the highest sale ($485,250).

reviewHighlights.formula: Median = Middle value in an ordered set
steps: 1. Order all data values from least to greatest
2. Odd count: The median is the exact center number
3. Even count: The median is the mean of the two middle numbers
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Mean, Median, and Mode is finding the median without ordering the data first — students pick the middle number straight from the list as given (for 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 they say the median is 7, the middle position in that original order) instead of sorting least to greatest (2, 4, 6, 7, 9) and finding the true middle value, 6. Before finalizing a median, always reorder the data smallest to largest, then count to the middle position — and if there is an even number of values, average the two middle numbers.

level2.stem: Data set: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. What is the median?
level2.explanation: With 6 values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
choiceFeedback: With an even count, take the average of the two middle values.
Don't add all values and divide—find the middle two values.
The two middle values are 6 and 8—what's their average?
hints: Count the values: there are 6, an even number — so no single value sits exactly in the middle.
With an even count, the median is the average of the TWO middle values. In an ordered list of 6, those are the 3rd and 4th.
The list is already ordered. Step 1: circle the 3rd and 4th values. Step 2: add them and divide by 2 — that result is the median.
level2.stemEs: Conjunto de datos: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. ¿Cuál es la mediana?
level2.explanationEs: Con 6 valores, la mediana es el promedio del 3.º y el 4.º valor: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores: hay 6, un número par, así que ningún valor queda exactamente en el medio.
Con una cantidad par, la mediana es el promedio de los DOS valores centrales. En una lista ordenada de 6, esos son el 3.º y el 4.º.
La lista ya está ordenada. Paso 1: encierra el 3.º y el 4.º valor. Paso 2: súmalos y divide entre 2; ese resultado es la mediana.

level3.prompt: A basketball player scored 15, 18, 16, 42, and 14 points in 5 games. Find the mean and median. Which better represents the player's typical game? Explain how the outlier affects each measure.
level3.sentenceFrame: Mean = ___. Median = ___. The ___ better represents a typical game because the outlier (___) pulls the ___ toward it, making it ___ than most scores. The median is not affected because ___.
level3.hint: Start by adding all the scores, then divide by how many games were played.
hints: One game (42 points) is far above the others — that's your outlier. Keep it in mind as you find both measures.
Plan: (1) mean = sum of the 5 scores ÷ 5, (2) median = middle of the ordered scores, (3) decide which lands closer to most games.
Step 1: add 15 + 18 + 16 + 42 + 14 and divide by 5. Then order the scores least to greatest and circle the 3rd — compare the two results.
level3.explanation: The five scores add to 105, so the mean is 105 ÷ 5 = 21, while the ordered list 14, 15, 16, 18, 42 gives a median of 16. The 42-point game is an outlier that drags the mean up above four of the five games, but the median only cares about position, so 16 better represents a typical game.
level3.explanationEs: Los cinco puntajes suman 105, así que la media es 105 ÷ 5 = 21, mientras que la lista ordenada 14, 15, 16, 18, 42 da una mediana de 16. El juego de 42 puntos es un valor atípico que jala la media por encima de cuatro de los cinco juegos, pero a la mediana solo le importa la posición, así que 16 representa mejor un juego típico.
level3.promptEs: Un jugador de baloncesto anotó 15, 18, 16, 42 y 14 puntos en 5 partidos. Encuentra la media y la mediana. ¿Cuál representa mejor un partido típico del jugador? Explica cómo afecta el valor atípico a cada medida.
hintsEs: Un partido (42 puntos) está muy por encima de los demás: ese es tu valor atípico. Tenlo presente al hallar ambas medidas.
Plan: (1) media = suma de los 5 puntajes ÷ 5, (2) mediana = el medio de los puntajes ordenados, (3) decide cuál queda más cerca de la mayoría de los partidos.
Paso 1: suma 15 + 18 + 16 + 42 + 14 y divide entre 5. Luego ordena los puntajes de menor a mayor, encierra el 3.º y compara los dos resultados.
